```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r}
library(z3r)
ctx <- z3_context()
```

Z3 strings are Unicode sequences. R character values convert to them
exactly, escapes and all, and results come back as UTF-8.

## String constraints

```{r}
s <- z3_string(ctx, "s")
t <- z3_string(ctx, "t")
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol,
  z3_concat(s, "-", t) == "alpha-beta",
  z3_length(s) > z3_length(t) - 2,
  z3_prefixof("al", s))
z3_check(sol)
m <- z3_model(sol)
c(s = z3_value(z3_eval(m, s)), t = z3_value(z3_eval(m, t)))
```

Positions are 0-based, as in SMT-LIB:

```{r}
hello <- z3_string_val(ctx, "hello")
val <- function(e) z3_value(z3_simplify(e))
c(substr = val(z3_substr(hello, 1, 3)), at = val(z3_str_at(hello, 4)),
  index = val(z3_indexof(hello, "l")), last = val(z3_last_indexof(hello, "l")),
  replace = val(z3_replace(hello, "l", "L")))
val(z3_str_to_int(z3_string_val(ctx, "1234")))
val(z3_int_to_str(z3_int_val(ctx, 99)))
```

`escaped = TRUE` reads SMT-LIB escapes such as `\u{e9}`, and
`z3_string_escaped()` writes them back. Raw vectors convert both ways for
strings whose characters are all below U+0100:

```{r}
cafe <- z3_string_val(ctx, "caf\\u{e9}", escaped = TRUE)
z3_value(cafe) == "caf\u00e9"
z3_string_escaped(cafe)
z3_string_bytes(z3_string_val(ctx, "Z3"))
```

## Regular expressions

Regular expressions are built from strings and combinators; a plain string
is accepted wherever a regular expression is expected:

```{r}
digit <- z3_re_range("0", "9", ctx)
lower <- z3_re_range("a", "z", ctx)
id <- z3_re_concat(z3_re_plus(lower), "_", z3_re_loop(digit, 2, 4))
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_in_re(s, id), z3_length(s) == 8, z3_contains(s, "zz"))
z3_check(sol)
z3_value(z3_eval(z3_model(sol), s))
```

Regular expressions also prove properties. A character that is not a digit
is "any character" intersected with the complement of the digits; no
non-empty number is made only of such characters:

```{r}
any_char <- z3_re_allchar(z3_re_sort(z3_string_sort(ctx)))
non_digit <- z3_re_intersect(any_char, z3_re_complement(digit))
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_in_re(s, z3_re_plus(digit)), z3_in_re(s, z3_re_star(non_digit)))
z3_check(sol)
```

Note that `z3_re_complement(digit)` alone is every string except the
one-character digit strings, including `"12"`; the intersection with
`any_char` restricts it to single characters.

## A password policy

A policy written as a regular expression: an uppercase letter, four to six
lowercase letters, two or three digits, and `!` or `?`.

```{r}
pw <- z3_string(ctx, "pw")
upper <- z3_re_range("A", "Z", ctx)
policy <- z3_re_concat(upper, z3_re_loop(lower, 4, 6), z3_re_loop(digit, 2, 3),
                       z3_re_union(z3_string_val(ctx, "!"), "?"))
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_in_re(pw, policy), z3_length(pw) == 9,
       z3_prefixof("R", pw), z3_suffixof("!", pw))
z3_check(sol)
z3_value(z3_eval(z3_model(sol), pw))
```

The policy cannot produce a 14-character password:

```{r}
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_in_re(pw, policy), z3_length(pw) == 14)
z3_check(sol)
```

## Characters

```{r, eval = z3_version_at_least("4.8.15")}
lambda <- z3_char_val(ctx, 955)
lambda
z3_value(z3_simplify(z3_char_to_int(lambda)))
z3_value(z3_simplify(z3_str_from_code(z3_int_val(ctx, 955))))
z3_value(z3_simplify(z3_char_is_digit(z3_char_val(ctx, 55))))
```

## Sequences of any sort

The same operations work on sequences of integers, Booleans, or any other
sort:

```{r}
I <- z3_int_sort(ctx)
q <- z3_const(ctx, "q", z3_seq_sort(I))
u <- function(v) z3_seq_unit(z3_int_val(ctx, v))
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_length(q) == 4, z3_seq_nth(q, 0) == 9,
       z3_contains(q, z3_concat(u(1), u(2))), z3_suffixof(u(5), q))
z3_check(sol)
z3_eval(z3_model(sol), q)
```

Newer Z3 releases add higher-order sequence functions, whose function
argument is a lambda:

```{r, eval = z3_version_at_least("4.13.2")}
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
z3_simplify(z3_seq_map(z3_lambda(x, x * 10), z3_concat(u(1), u(2), u(3))))
acc <- z3_int(ctx, "acc")
r <- z3_int(ctx, "r")
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, r == z3_seq_foldl(z3_lambda(list(acc, x), acc + x), 0, z3_concat(u(4), u(5), u(6))))
z3_check(sol)
z3_eval(z3_model(sol), r)
```

```{r, eval = z3_version_at_least("4.15.5")}
z3_value(z3_simplify(z3_replace_all(z3_string_val(ctx, "a-b-c"), "-", "+")))
```

String solving is decidable only for fragments; with lengths, conversions
to integers and regular expressions together, `"unknown"` answers are
possible.
